markdown_report:
### Insights

**Starting point.** (1) Feedback favors repeated recent interests over broad associations, motivating a transition control without treating feedback as observed intent. (2) Training margins depend on score scale and sampled negatives; rank-based interventions provide complementary evidence. (3) Missing specifications and needs remain unknown, never incompatibility or rejection labels.

**Related work.** (1) Spotify evaluates pairwise models against Transformers using full-catalog NDCG@10; its results motivate controls, not predicted RecHarness gains. PCTM uses uniform-prior smoothing plus separate popularity adjustment. (2) CoDeR motivates demand-shift hypotheses, but history interventions cannot identify causal preferences. (3) Sampling research cautions that sampled and full-catalog conclusions can differ. Candidate-local normalization also changes fusion weights; frozen training-derived scales avoid this inconsistency.

### Framework and directions

| Direction | Existing approach | Gap and proposed response |
|---|---|---|
| Recent evidence | SASRec; pairwise controls | Test transition residual against popularity residual |
| Ranking supervision | Sampled BCE; gSASRec | Compare corrected loss under actual sampling |
| Diagnostic validity | Margins; history interventions | Measure paired rank changes, coverage, and uncertainty |
| Consistent fusion | Candidate-local normalization | Freeze training-derived scales and denominators |

### Candidate ideas

Scores are originality/potential/code difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

1. **Fixed-scale transition residual: 3/6/4.** Blend SASRec with recent transition evidence. Originality: useful integration, but established components. Potential: interpretable and cheap, but sparse support and popularity confounding limit claims. Difficulty: no encoder retraining, but calibration, controls, and predictor parity require care.
2. **Generalized-BCE replacement: 3/6/3.** Apply gSASRec’s correction. Originality: principled, but existing. Potential: addresses overconfidence, but calibration need not improve HR@10. Difficulty: localized changes, but sampling parameters must match.
3. **Intervention-guided recency regularization: 6/6/6.** Encourage full-history/suffix agreement where training-prefix targets support both. Originality: connects diagnosis to training, but resembles consistency learning. Potential: reduces stale-history dependence, but may erase long-term interests. Difficulty: reuses the encoder, but needs extra passes and causal masking.

### Selected idea: recent-transition residual

At 0% progress, retain this feasible hypothesis with stronger controls. Build smoothed directed adjacent-transition counts from training histories; aggregate the last three items with exponential recency weights. Freeze category-specific score scales estimated on deterministic training-only queries. Score each item independently of candidate composition and chunk boundaries.

Compare SASRec, SASRec+popularity, and SASRec+transition using three prespecified nonzero strengths and identical validation candidates. Retain baseline on ties. Treat SASRec+both and smoothing/history ablations as subsequent, explicitly budgeted experiments.

Report category and macro HR@10, transition support, and paired user-bootstrap uncertainty. Diagnostic count tables must exclude their target occurrences; neural training-prefix results remain training diagnostics. Distinguish sensitivity from prediction improvement and popularity shortcuts from transition evidence.

Preserve routing, seeds, paths, the 200-epoch environment default, both diagnostic entry points, and predictor-writer parity. Record unavailable measurements with reasons and counts. Repeated validation selection can overfit; freeze the small search before evaluation. No improvement is claimed.

idea.description: Add a sparse, recency-weighted item-transition residual to each per-dataset SASRec predictor, using frozen training-derived score scales. Compare against an equally tuned popularity residual and the unchanged baseline using pinned macro validation HR@10.
idea.motivation: Qualitative feedback suggests that broad associations sometimes overwhelm specific recent interests. Transition evidence tests a narrow hypothesis using observed histories alone, while a popularity control tests whether any gain merely reflects destination frequencies. Neither component establishes compatibility, satisfied ownership, simulator traits, rejection, or immediate intent. The original candidate-local standardization was a methodological gap: candidate-dependent standard deviations can reverse fused pairwise rankings between sampled evaluation and full-catalog recommendations.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four dataset routes, prescribed input splits, single-GPU execution, and artifacts beneath the trial directory. Respect SASREC_EPOCHS with environment default 200. Do not inspect hidden test files or fetch datasets or pretrained weights. The restricted task contract overrides the generic metadata examples: use only public histories, timestamps, titles, and descriptions; review ratings/text and item ratings/categories/prices/stores are unavailable.

Build adjacent directed counts C(i,j) from each user's training history in its prescribed order, excluding padding. Let f(j) count all nonpadding training interactions, p(j)=f(j)/sum_k f(k), and d(i)=sum_j C(i,j). Prespecify smoothing alpha=10 and P(j|i)=[C(i,j)+alpha*p(j)]/[d(i)+alpha]. This is a popularity-prior model, not Spotify's PCTM. For the last m=min(3, history_length) nonpadding items, assign age a=0 to the newest and normalized weights exp(-a)/sum_b exp(-b). Define t(h,j)=sum_a w_a P(j|i_a). An empty history uses p(j). Missing source rows also back off to p(j). Keep denominators fixed over the declared category catalog, never the requested candidate subset. Store sparse counts and compute the popularity contribution analytically without densifying the transition matrix.

After fitting each SASRec model, construct a reproducible calibration reference using only training data: sort users by their canonical string IDs, enumerate prefixes with at least one observed item and a following training item, sample up to 1,024 prefixes without replacement using a local NumPy generator seeded 42, and sample 128 distinct nonpadding catalog items per prefix, or the entire catalog if smaller, using that generator. Calibration uses scores only, not target correctness, and these are explicitly in-sample scale estimates. In evaluation mode, calculate population standard deviations sigma_s, sigma_t, and sigma_p over the pooled reference pairs for SASRec logits, transition scores, and popularity scores. Freeze them separately per category with floor 1e-8; record means, raw variances, reference counts, seed, and catalog identity for auditing. A channel with exactly zero reference variance is disabled. Centering by the frozen mean is optional because it adds an item-independent constant; implement one shared formula everywhere. Never normalize over evaluation candidates or inference chunks. Calibration prefix enumeration must be bounded or reservoir-sampled if its materialization would exceed available CPU memory.

Use S(h,j)=s(h,j)/sigma_s+lambda*t(h,j)/sigma_t for the transition arm, and replace t by p for the popularity arm. Baseline scores remain raw SASRec logits. Prespecify lambda in {0.1,0.3,1.0} for each arm, plus the shared baseline: seven configurations, with equal tuning budgets for the two residuals. Each configuration includes all four categories and uses one common lambda; do not separately tune category strengths. Select the greatest pinned macro validation HR@10. Resolve exact ties by baseline first, then smaller lambda, then popularity before transition. Reuse the host's users, candidates, exclusions, routing, and tie behavior without recreating or changing its evaluator. If the host exposes evaluation only by running predictors, emit the corresponding frozen configurations for that authorized workflow rather than assuming an internal evaluation API. Score raw fused values directly.

Reserve additional ablations for a subsequent prespecified budget: SASRec+both; transition-only and popularity-only; unsmoothed, uniform-prior, and popularity-prior smoothing; last-item, equally weighted, and recency-weighted aggregation; directed transitions versus unordered co-occurrence; source-independent destination counts; and histories shuffled while preserving each user's item multiset. For the unsmoothed arm, define zero-support rows explicitly as zero transition evidence. Give compared arms equal tuning budgets and their own frozen calibration scales. A gain beyond SASRec+popularity, accompanied by loss of advantage after transition destruction and consistent popularity-stratified results, strengthens the transition interpretation without proving causality. These ablations are proposed controls, not measured findings or prerequisites for the initial seven-configuration screen.

Report per-category HR@10 and their equal-weight macro average, source-row support, direct pair-support rate, backoff frequency, and popularity strata defined from training frequencies. If per-user validation hits are available, use 2,000 paired bootstrap replicates with local seed 42, resampling users within each category and equally averaging category means. Report percentile 95% intervals for paired changes. These intervals condition on fitted models, fixed candidates, and selected configurations; they exclude training variability and adaptive-selection uncertainty. Do not infer significance from these intervals after unrestricted search. Keep full-catalog diagnostics separate from sampled selection metrics. No numerical gain, uncertainty interval, or preference label may be invented.

Store model architecture configuration, sparse counts, row totals, training frequencies, smoothing and recency settings, frozen scales, selected arm and lambda, and catalog mappings beneath the trial directory. Update the predictor writer so working/predict.py loads the actual trained architecture and all four routes and uses the same scorer for sampled and full-catalog requests. Preserve existing eligibility masks and evaluator tie handling. Verify that scoring an item alone, in candidate subsets, or in different chunk sizes gives the same fused score within floating-point tolerance. Algebraic candidate independence does not imply identical HR@10 across different competitor sets.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), embedding measured metrics and definitions into its interpretation prompt. view.model must reference the trained nn.Module. Preserve view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, and review_data compatibility. Keep neural-logit margins explicitly separate from fused-ranking diagnostics; the latter require the actual sequence prefix to compute transition evidence. Use inference_mode and restore view.model.training in a finally block. Bound diagnostics to the first ten batches, mask zero targets and positions without preceding real history, report counts, and return undefined/null measurements with reasons for empty samples. Leave unavailable category lists empty and mark them unavailable. Embedding alignment remains an embedding statistic, not recommendation diversity. A fixed 0.5 margin threshold remains scale-dependent and cannot certify ranking quality.

Training-prefix count diagnostics must remove direct target contamination. For every queried adjacent training occurrence i→j, use a temporary count view with that occurrence subtracted from C(i,j), d(i), f(j), and the total frequency used by the popularity prior; preserve independent occurrences of the same pair. Recompute every affected probability used for the prefix, not just the most recent source row. Skip diagnostics when subtraction makes required totals undefined. This leave-one-occurrence-out construction is for adjacent counts only; windowed statistics would require removing every contribution exposing the target. It does not make the neural model out-of-sample and does not establish temporal validity when other users' later events remain in the table. Label these limitations explicitly. For deployment validation, construct statistics from the prescribed training split only, without diagnostic subtraction or altered splits.

For every per-position diagnostic query predicting x[t+1], construct sequence features, recency weights, and lengths from x[1:t] only. Verify in evaluation mode that changing an appended suffix leaves prefix representations and scores unchanged. Any pooled representation must obey the same truncation rule despite causal attention elsewhere. Training-prefix intervention comparisons may retain recent suffixes, delete recent events, shuffle while fixing the last item, or remove repeated title/description themes, with equal-count position/popularity-matched random controls and fixed candidates. Report paired target-rank changes, HR@10 changes, and top-10 overlap as training diagnostics; they are not evidence of genuine user intent. Measure evidence coverage and unknown rates instead of inferring unsupported compatibility or redundancy. Keep the twenty simulator users, five per category, on full-catalog unseen-item recommendations; simulator feedback does not replace macro validation HR@10 for selection. Account for training, calibration, diagnostics, debugging, ablations, and failed trials within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget.
idea.pseudocode:
DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']
FOUR_DATASETS = [Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl]

for dataset in FOUR_DATASETS:
    model = train_baseline_sasrec(
        dataset, preprocessing_seed=0, training_seed=42,
        epochs=int(os.environ.get('SASREC_EPOCHS', '200')))
    C, row_totals, frequency = count_adjacent_training_transitions(dataset.user_train)
    reference = deterministic_training_prefix_candidate_pairs(
        dataset, seed=42, max_prefixes=1024, candidates_per_prefix=128)
    scales = population_score_stds(
        model, C, row_totals, frequency, reference,
        alpha=10, recent_limit=3, age_decay=1,
        epsilon=1e-8, disable_exactly_constant_channels=True)
    save_all_artifacts_beneath_trial(dataset, model, C, row_totals, frequency, scales)

function score(sequence, candidates, dataset, configuration):
    base = dataset.model.predict(sequence, candidates)
    if configuration.arm == 'baseline':
        return base
    if configuration.arm == 'popularity':
        residual = training_frequency_probability(candidates)
        residual_scale = dataset.scales.popularity
    else:
        residual = recency_weighted_smoothed_transition_scores(
            last_nonpadding_items(sequence, limit=3), candidates,
            alpha=10, fixed_catalog_denominators=True)
        residual_scale = dataset.scales.transition
    return base / dataset.scales.sasrec + configuration.lambda * residual / residual_scale
    # Disabled constant channels contribute zero; scales never depend on candidates.

configurations = [baseline] + [
    configuration(arm, lambda)
    for arm in ['popularity', 'transition']
    for lambda in [0.1, 0.3, 1.0]
]
# Run configurations through the existing authorized host evaluation workflow.
for configuration in configurations:
    write_predictor_for_all_four_routes(configuration)
    result[configuration] = existing_pinned_host_validation_result()
chosen = greatest_macro_HR10_with_prespecified_tiebreak(result)
write_predictor_loading_actual_models_and_frozen_artifacts(chosen)
verify_candidate_subset_and_chunk_score_invariance()

class DiagnosisProbe:
    run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
        prior_mode = view.model.training
        try:
            view.model.eval()
            with inference_mode():
                for batch in first_ten_batches(train_loader):
                    for valid_position in batch:
                        prefix = sequence_through_current_position_only()
                        target = next_training_item()
                        measure_neural_training_margin(prefix, target, loader_negative)
                        diagnostic_counts = subtract_one_target_occurrence_and_all_affected_marginals()
                        measure_transition_support_and_fused_training_ranking(
                            prefix, target, diagnostic_counts, frozen_scales)
                report_counts_undefined_reasons_and_metric_limitations()
        finally:
            view.model.train(prior_mode)
        return {metrics: measured_values_and_counts,
                metric_definitions: definitions_and_limitations}

function diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return prompt_containing(
        raw_diagnosis.metrics, raw_diagnosis.metric_definitions,
        'Distinguish measurements from hypotheses; preserve unavailable evidence; '
        'do not infer causal intent, user traits, compatibility, or rejection.')

originality.positive: The proposal connects an explicit diagnostic hypothesis to a reproducible residual comparison with candidate-independent calibration and a matched popularity control.
originality.negative: Transitions, recency weighting, smoothing, frozen scaling, and score blending are established techniques; the combination warrants a lower originality rating than the original report.

future_potential.positive: A cheap, interpretable control can identify when recent transition evidence adds value and guide later architecture or supervision changes.
future_potential.negative: Sparse support, popularity backoff, sampled-evaluation effects, and finite validation reuse limit generalization claims; no matched-task improvement has been measured.

code_difficulty.positive: The residual requires sparse counting and scoring without additional encoder training, and frozen scales simplify streamed inference.
code_difficulty.negative: Reproducible calibration, popularity controls, contamination-aware diagnostics, artifact serialization, and predictor-writer parity make implementation moderately harder than the original rating suggested.

related_work.title: Do sequential recommendation benchmarks require higher-order sequence modelling? — Spotify Research
contributions: The supplied account compares MC, FMC, FMC+, SeqRules, PCTM, sampled-softmax SASRec, and eSASRec using full-catalog NDCG@10 on Amazon Beauty/Sports/Toys and MovieLens-1M/20M.
Pairwise probes outperform both Transformers on four datasets; eSASRec wins ML-20M, motivating inexpensive pairwise controls.
PCTM uses uniform-prior smoothing and a separate popularity adjustment.
limitations: These results do not establish transition-residual gains over SASRec+popularity or predict performance on the four RecHarness categories with sampled HR@10.
The proposed popularity-prior transition model is not an implementation of PCTM.

related_work.title: Spotify sequential-capacity-probes — official implementations and results
contributions: Provides implementation references for the pairwise and Transformer comparison described in the supplied search results.
limitations: Its evaluation protocol differs from the pinned RecHarness protocol; implementation details must not silently replace task splits, candidates, or scoring.

related_work.title: CoDeR — AAAI 2025
contributions: The supplied summary describes demand extraction and counterfactual adjustment for demand shifts obscured by noise and bias.
limitations: History sensitivity does not establish causal preference change or validate inferred user intent.

related_work.title: gSASRec — IJCAI 2024
contributions: Connects sampled binary-cross-entropy training to overconfidence and motivates a corrected-loss comparison.
limitations: Better calibration does not guarantee improved pinned HR@10; correction parameters must match the actual sampling configuration.

related_work.title: On the Reliability of Sampling Strategies — RecSys 2025
contributions: Examines how sampled evaluation affects resolution, robustness, and agreement with full evaluation.
limitations: Does not justify changing pinned candidate sampling or substituting another selection metric.
Frozen score scales address fusion consistency, not sampled-rank estimation bias.

related_work.title: On the Bias of Offline Evaluation Methods for Recommender Systems — sampling analysis
contributions: Supports distinguishing sampled-candidate evaluation conclusions from full-catalog ranking conclusions.
limitations: Does not establish which proposed residual will improve the matched RecHarness task.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation — SASRec
contributions: Provides the causal sequential-recommendation baseline and per-position next-item modeling framework.
limitations: Causal attention alone does not prevent leakage introduced by future-aware pooling or incorrectly constructed prefix features.

related_work.title: Leakage study supplied in reflection results
contributions: Motivates explicit auditing of target contamination and information availability in diagnostic statistics.
limitations: The proposed leave-one-occurrence-out count protocol is a task-specific design, not a claim that this source validates the complete diagnostic procedure.
Removing a target occurrence does not remove neural training exposure or ensure global temporal validity.

related_work.title: Reciprocal rank fusion outperforms Condorcet and individual rank learning methods
contributions: Provides a rank-based alternative to score calibration.
limitations: Candidate-local component ranks remain candidate-dependent; consistent restriction requires ranks computed over a shared full-catalog universe.
Full-catalog rank computation adds cost, so frozen score scales remain the initial choice.

related_work.title: Mergeable Welford statistics — implementation reference
contributions: Illustrates mergeable streaming statistics suitable for accumulating score means and variances without retaining all scores.
limitations: This is a computational reference, not evidence of recommendation gains.
Query-adaptive global normalization would require an identical catalog universe and shared statistics across all chunks; it is more expensive than the selected frozen-scale approach.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation — Cawley and Talbot
contributions: Explains how repeated model selection can overfit finite validation data, supporting a small prespecified comparison.
limitations: A limited sweep reduces search flexibility but does not eliminate selection bias; conditional user-bootstrap intervals do not account for adaptive search.
